newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Delta to double ex-Amsterdam capacity.
newsitem.headline: Delta to double ex-Amsterdam capacity.

text.p: Delta Airlines will double its cargo capacity ex-Netherlands from June 2, Jos van der Woensel, managing director of Zygene, Delta's Netherlands general sales agent, said on Wednesday.
Under the U.S. airline's existing schedule, Amsterdam is served along with Stuttgart and Prague.

Delta is currently flying Atlanta-Amsterdam-Stuttgart and New York-Amsterdam-Prague but from June 2 Amsterdam will get its own direct services. Stuttgart flights will then be operated along with Frankfurt and Prague will then be teamed-up with Copenhagen.
Delta Airlines will fly daily Lockheed L1011 TriStar services to Atlanta and New York from Schiphol, with 12 tonnes capacity on each flight, said Van der Woensel.
The airline also trucks cargo from Amsterdam to Paris and Frankfurt.
He said that the North American market is booming currently and he is confident that the extra capacity will be easily filled.
The dollar's strength is helping to stimulate ex-Europe business, he added.
